steps.content:
PLAN
1. List the directory and read the files named in the task.
2. Create a new file named `harness_fuzz.c` in the root of the repository.
3. Include the `src/tlv.h` header file in `harness_fuzz.c`.
4. Define the `int LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput(const uint8_t *data, size_t size)` function.
5. Declare a `TlvDoc doc` variable and call `tlv_parse(data, size, &doc)`.
6. On `TLV_OK`, call `tlv_free(&doc)` and `tlv_total_len_of_type(&doc, data[0])`.
7. Compile the harness with `clang -fsanitize=fuzzer,address,undefined harness_fuzz.c src/tlv.c -I . -o /tmp/h`.
8. Fix any errors in the harness file.
9. Run the FuzzVerifier to ensure the harness builds and executes correctly.

The failure indicates that the `data` and `size` variables are not declared in the `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` function. To fix this, declare these variables at the beginning of the function.

ACTION: edit_file
```json
{
  "path": "harness_fuzz.c",
  "search": "int LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput(const uint8_t *data, size_t size) {",
  "replace": "int LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput(const uint8_t *data, size_t size) {\n    TlvDoc doc;\n    tlv_status status = tlv_parse(data, size, &doc);\n    if (status == TLV_OK) {\n        tlv_free(&doc);\n        tlv_total_len_of_type(&doc, data[0]);\n    }\n    return 0;\n}"
}
```

The failure indicates that the `data` and `size` variables are not declared in the `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` function, and there is a redefinition of the `status` variable. To fix this, declare the `data` and `size` variables at the beginning of the function and ensure that the `status` variable is not redefined.

ACTION: edit_file
```json
{
  "path": "harness_fuzz.c",
  "search": "int LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput(const uint8_t *data, size_t size) {",
  "replace": "int LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput(const uint8_t *data, size_t size) {\n    TlvDoc doc;\n    tlv_status status = tlv_parse(data, size, &doc);\n    if (status == TLV_OK) {\n        tlv_free(&doc);\n        tlv_total_len_of_type(&doc, data[0]);\n    }\n    return 0;\n}"
}
```
